key_insight: Optimized smooth flux pulses enable 12-ns transmon CZ gates with intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵, while revealing operating regimes resilient to dephasing.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps superconducting-processor designers balance gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness, potentially reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.
method: Optimize single-shot flux pulses for directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons.
Model intrinsic Hamiltonian errors, energy relaxation, and fast and slow dephasing.
Identify dephasing sweet spots and exploit transmon asymmetry for noise-resilient operation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 12-ns gates versus an 11.6-ns theoretical speed limit, intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵, and dephasing models calibrated against published experimental measurements.
watch_item: The reported intrinsic error is not the total error under decoherence; hardware performance and recalibration savings require experimental validation.
paper_title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
